name: Ryu SDN Framework
what_it_is: Ryu is a component-based Software Defined Networking (SDN) framework written in Python that provides well-defined APIs for developers to create network management and control applications. It supports multiple OpenFlow versions and related protocols such as NETCONF and OF-config.
components: OpenFlow protocol library (v1.0, v1.2, v1.3, v1.4, v1.5, Nicira Extensions)
BGP speaker with SSH console (requires paramiko)
Zebra protocol service with SQLAlchemy database backend
configuration: Optional OF-config support via lxml and ncclient packages
Optional NETCONF support via paramiko package
Optional BGP speaker SSH console via paramiko package
Optional Zebra protocol database via SQLAlchemy package
Applications passed as arguments to ryu-manager at launch
modes: Component-based application mode (custom apps loaded as modules)
constraints: Ryu is not currently maintained and actively seeks new maintainers — stability and security fixes are not guaranteed
Entire framework is Python-only; no compiled controller core, which limits raw packet-processing throughput
NETCONF and OF-config functionality require optional third-party packages (paramiko, lxml, ncclient) not installed by default
No built-in high-availability or redundancy mechanisms documented
notable_absences: No docker-compose.yml present in the repository
No built-in measurement or telemetry collection
No fault injection or chaos-testing utilities
No documented scalability limits or topology size constraints
